newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PAKISTAN COTTON RATES STABLE ON BUYING BY MILLS.
newsitem.headline: PAKISTAN COTTON RATES STABLE ON BUYING BY MILLS.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates stayed stable on Thursday with demand from mills and dealers said prices would remain firm in the coming weeks as arrival of fresh supplies had not fully picked up.

"Mostly mills from Punjab (province) are buyers in Sindh (province)," dealer Khushi Ram said. "Right now demand exceeds supply. New cotton arrival (1997/98 July-June) in the Punjab is expected to start in September, while in Sindh it will take another few weeks before it comes into full swing."
In the kerb, new-crop NIAB-78 variety was traded at around 2,260 rupees ($55.63) per maund (37.32 kg).
